turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Right, Mr Hale, quick check before you go in. Blood pressure is one thirty eight over eighty two, pulse 76, sats ninety six percent on air.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm. Took long enough. I've been sat in that corridor since half eight.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sorry about the wait. On the repeat list I've got ramapril five milligrams once a day for the blood pressure.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): It's ramipril, and it's ten, not five. Chemist upped it. Five was donkey's years ago. Still once a day, yeah, for the blood pressure.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I'll flag that. And atorvastatin twenty milligrams at night for the cholesterol, that's current?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Twenty. Don't miss that one.
[SEG0007] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Lovely. Doctor's free, I'll pop you through.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mr Hale, thanks for waiting. I'm Dr Shah. What's brought you down today?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): The cough. Every single morning I'm coughing up this brown muck. I'm tired of it, and I'm tired full stop, so can we not drag this out.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Brown stuff in the mornings. How long's that been going on, do you reckon?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): umm. Years. err, honestly I couldn't tell you when it started. Well before I packed the fags in, anyway.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): When did you stop smoking?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Last year. March. Just stopped. Still fancy one when the van's playing up, but I haven't had one.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): You still driving for work?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Vans. Early starts, which is when this cough is worst, sat in the cab hacking away. Parking here was a nightmare as well, don't get me started.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain with it?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No pain in the chest. Just the cough and what comes up.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever, temperatures?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't get fevers. I'm just irritable 'cause I've been hanging about, that's all.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Has your weight changed?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Same. Same belt hole. Wife would've noticed, she notices everything.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): And when you walk, up a slope or carrying stuff, how is the breathing?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Bit. I don't know. well, actually maybe on the stairs, but I'm sixty four and I don't sprint. Not gasping. Hard to say.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right, we'll leave that open. Have you been given anything for the cough?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): They tried that mucus one, I always say it wrong, carbo, carbocisteine. Two capsules three times a day. I stopped it in March. Did nothing except make us feel sick.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stopped in March, ok. And the brown inhaler on the old letter?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Never took it. Never even picked it up from the chemist. So that doesn't count.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines, or anything else?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing I know of.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me listen to your chest. Deep breath... and out. Again.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Chest expansion is fine. Few crackles at the right base, no wheeze. Heart sounds are normal. Ankles aren't swollen.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): So is it bad?

[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm thinking out loud here. Long morning cough, brown phlegm, you quit last year, and the chest is mostly quiet apart from those crackles. My working impression is chronic bronchitis. Could be early COPD, I can't say that properly without numbers. Doesn't look like a chest infection today, no fever, weight steady.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): COPD. Great. My brother had that and he was on oxygen. Don't tell me I'm heading there.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm not saying that. Different people, different lungs. We measure first, that's the whole point.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. What are you actually going to do, then.

[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll book spirometry for Tuesday morning, nine o'clock, with the respiratory nurse. That's the blowing test, shows if the airways are narrowed. No fasting for that one, just turn up.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Tuesday. That's my early round. Ugh. Alright.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): And uh bloods Thursday morning here, fasting, water only. Full blood count and kidney function, because of the ramipril. Take the ramipril after the bloods, not before.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday as well. Two trips. Brilliant.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the spirometry comes back borderline, then we do a CT of the chest. I'm not booking that now. Only if the numbers sit in the middle.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): And if they're fine?
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): If they're clearly normal or clearly obstructed we may not need the scan at all. I'll see you back in two weeks with the results either way.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks. More waiting.

[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): One more thing. With the smoking history I'd like you to get the flu jab and the pneumococcal one at your practice, this autumn is fine. And please don't go back to the cigarettes, even when the van's playing up.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): The jabs I can do. The fags, yeah, I hear you. Can I go?
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): You can. Reception will have the Tuesday and Thursday times on a slip.

spec.situation: Former smoker who quit last year with a long-standing morning cough and brown phlegm; weight stable; no chest pain; spirometry planned; vaccination advice.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

bad.reason: Hypertension implied by ramipril for blood pressure, but reported_by is staff and patient, not patient only.
Bloods Thursday morning for FBC and kidney function because of ramipril; cough assessment indication not stated.
bad.text: Blood tests (type=laboratory, status=planned, requested_by=doctor, indication=Cough assessment and renal monitoring on ramipril, scheduled_datetime=Thursday morning)
